clearing_status.fact: SEC granted a first one-year extension on Feb 25, 2025 (Release No. 34-102487), moving cash deadline to Dec 31, 2026 and repo to Jun 30, 2027. On Apr 17, 2026, the SEC published SIFMA's request for exemptive relief (inter-affiliate exemption) with a May 29, 2026 comment deadline still open. No second extension announced as of late May 2026. Source: SEC.gov press release Feb 25, 2025; SEC Commissioner Uyeda statement Apr 20, 2026; TBAC Charge Q2 2026 (May 29, 2026).
clearing_status.rationale: One formal extension has already been granted (Feb 2025) and exemptive-relief requests from SIFMA are actively pending before the SEC (Apr 2026), satisfying two independent rubric-1 triggers. No evidence of a second extension or missed deadline exists, ruling out rubric-2.

plan_financing.fact: 10y JGB yield hit 3.055%-3.08% on Sep 24-25 2026 (30-year high since Aug 1996), up ~18bps over the prior month and cumulatively ~130bps since Takaichi fiscal stimulus plans emerged in late 2025. Most recent 10y auction (Sep 1) cleared with average bid-to-cover and the Sep 3 30y auction posted BTC of 3.79 (Bloomberg, 2026-09-03). The May 2026 supplementary budget (~3 trillion yen) pledged flat total bond issuance, but analysts flagged the financing path as not fully credible (CNBC, 2026-06-01). Sep 24 yield spike attributed partly to US Treasury global contagion (UOB/CNBC).
plan_financing.rationale: Yield is well above the 25bps threshold on fiscal concern (cumulative ~130bps since Takaichi stimulus), and the funding path credibility is contested; however, no auction has failed (BTC <2) or tailed severely, and no emergency BOJ operation has occurred, ruling out a score of 2 and placing this firmly in the UNCLEAR band.

dissent.view: Sep 24 yield spike to 3.055% driven primarily by US PMI data and weak US 5y Treasury auction (global contagion), not fresh Japan fiscal news — implying the fiscal-specific signal may be overstated

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings reported its trailing 12-month U.S. private credit default rate (inclusive of distressed exchanges, maturity extensions, and payment-in-kind switches) rose to a record 6.3% through August 2026, up from 6.1% in July, covering approximately 1,300-1,500 borrowers. Bloomberg/Fitch report dated September 14, 2026.
direct_lending_default.rationale: The Fitch PCDR — the rubric's mandated anchor — printed a new all-time high of 6.3% for August 2026 (published 14-Sep-2026), superseding the prior April/May record of 6.0%; 14 default events in August (highest monthly count in trailing 12 months) included stressed maturity extensions (45% of events) and PIK conversions, corroborating sustained funding stress in private credit plumbing.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index: 2.51% in Q2 2026 (count-based, 716 senior secured/unitranche loans, $195.6bn) — materially lower due to narrower definitional scope excluding many distressed exchanges
Moody's: 2025 headline private credit default rate 1.6%-4.7% excluding distressed restructurings; estimates distressed exchanges accounted for ~65% of all 2025 private credit defaults

Fitch model-based sub-component (CLO opinions series) stood at 5.6% in August vs. privately monitored ratings sub-component at 8.5%, illustrating internal spread within Fitch's own blended 6.3% composite

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings tracked 10 of 16 non-traded BDCs breaching their 5% quarterly repurchase caps in Q2 2026 (requests averaged 10.3% of NAV); named funds gated in the same quarter include Blackstone BCRED (~$79B AUM), Cliffwater Corporate Lending Fund (~$31B), Apollo Debt Solutions BDC, BlackRock Private Credit Fund, Ares Strategic Income Fund, HPS Corporate Lending Fund, Blue Owl OCIC/OTIC, and Morgan Stanley North Haven. Robert A. Stanger & Co. reported Q2 repurchase requests at 12.4% of NAV industry-wide, the highest on record, with sponsors fulfilling only 38% (~$5.9B of ~$15.6B requested). Source: Angel Investors Network citing Fitch Ratings data, August 20 2026; Trading Market Signals Private Credit Redemption Monitor, August 17 2026; CRE Daily/AltsWire/ABF Journal/White Law Group, June-August 2026.
redemption_gates.rationale: Named funds with active gates in Q2 2026 number well above 3 and their combined AUM vastly exceeds $100B (BCRED alone is ~$79B; Cliffwater ~$31B), satisfying the WIDESPREAD threshold of >=3 largest funds or gated AUM >$100B. Corroborating signals include a 23% YTD decline in VanEck BDC ETF (BIZD), manager equity selloffs (Blackstone -46%, Blue Owl -67% from peak), Fitch recording a 6.1% private credit default rate in July 2026, and Cox Capital mini-tender offers at 14-25% NAV discounts -- all consistent with genuine liquidity stress rather than routine gate mechanics.

new_imf_programs.fact: IMF FY2026 Annual Report (imf.org/annual-report/2026) states only 2 new nonprecautionary lending arrangements were approved in May 2025-April 2026; no new sovereign missed coupons or standstills found in the April-September 2026 trailing 6-month window across IMF.org news, S&P, or secondary sources. Active programs (Argentina EFF, El Salvador EFF, Ghana ECF exit) are continuations or completions of pre-existing arrangements, not new distress initiations in the window.
new_imf_programs.rationale: The rubric requires new IMF program initiations or missed coupons within the trailing 6 months; all distress-adjacent activity found (Argentina, El Salvador, Ghana) reflects ongoing pre-2026 arrangements under review, not new program approvals or sovereign payment failures, mapping to CALM (0). No fresh missed coupon or standstill event was identified in the window from any authoritative source.

dissent.view: Ethiopia's Eurobond exchange (from Dec 2023 default) was staged for completion in 2026 and if a new exchange/restructuring step occurred in the window it could constitute a continuing distress event, though no new missed payment was found; Deluair Consultancy (Apr 2026) notes 21 Sub-Saharan countries in active IMF programs and ~USD 100bn in external debt service due in 2026, suggesting elevated but not newly triggered distress.

china_ppi.fact: NBS press release dated 2026-09-10 (https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202609/t20260910_1965274.html): 'In August 2026, China's producer price index for industrial products (PPI) increased by 3.8% year on year and 0.4% month on month.'
china_ppi.rationale: The NBS official figure of +3.8% YoY for August 2026, released 2026-09-10, is the load-bearing fact; the rubric requires reporting the signed figure (positive here, indicating cost-push inflation) and flags large moves in either direction as price-spillover shocks — +3.8% is a meaningful positive reading that the scoring engine will evaluate for input-cost pressure exportable to trading partners.

dissent.view: Trading Economics page cached at Feb 2026 data showing -0.9% YoY; this reflects an outdated snapshot, not a competing current reading

trade_actions.fact: In the trailing 3 months (Jul-Sep 2026) at least 6 confirmed new major-economy trade measures against Chinese goods were imposed or opened: (1) US 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariff on all Chinese goods, effective 24 Jul 2026 (USTR/Federal Register, 23 Jul 2026); (2) EU definitive AD duties on Chinese car/lorry tyres 4.3-45.3%, EU Reg 2026/1540, 8 Jul 2026 (EC trade policy site); (3) EU definitive AD on ferrosilicon from China, EU Reg 2026/1794, 27 Jul 2026; (4) EU definitive AD on synthetic polyamide yarns from China, EU Reg 2026/1823, 27 Jul 2026; (5) EU provisional AD on sodium benzoate from China, EU Reg 2026/1854, ~Aug 2026; (6) South Africa new 52.34% safeguard on Chinese flat-rolled steel, Jun 2026 + 5 AD amendment notices 18 Sep 2026 (ITAC Report 778/768). The US-China economic truce was extended 2 months to 10 Jan 2027 on 23 Sep 2026, and a bilateral tariff-cut list (77 US categories, 1,619 Chinese categories) was published 28 Sep 2026 but with no rates or dates set.
trade_actions.rationale: Six or more distinct new tariff/AD measures by major economies against China in the trailing 3-month window far exceeds the rubric threshold of >=4 measures for ESCALATING=2; the US broad 12.5% Section 301 rate across all Chinese goods also qualifies as a broad tariff round >=10% across a sector. The truce extension and tariff-cut list publication introduce some de-escalation signal but do not reverse any of the measures already imposed, so the rubric cap-at-evidence rule does not reduce the rating.

license_flow.fact: China's April 2025 MOFCOM licensing regime (Announcement No. 18) on seven heavy/medium rare earth elements and derived magnet products remains fully in force; approvals are issued case-by-case (per-shipment) with actual processing times of 60-120 days against a statutory 45-working-day target; a first batch of general licences was issued in December 2025 to only three major Chinese magnet makers (JL MAG, San Huan, Yunsheng) but is not broadly available; and the January 2026 Export Licensing Catalogue added samarium, gadolinium and lutetium compounds as new controlled categories. Trump threats of 200% tariffs in August 2026 and a ~21% year-on-year drop in magnet export volumes confirm ongoing throughput friction. Sources: China Briefing (Jul 27 2026), gettransport.com (Jul 7 2026), discoveryalert.com (Sep 2026), rare-earth-mining.com (Apr 2026).
license_flow.rationale: The regime fits Rubric 1 on all three triggers simultaneously: licensing is case-by-case (not blanket), typical processing exceeds 30 days (routinely 60-120 days in practice), and new categories (samarium, gadolinium, lutetium compounds) were added to the control list within the trailing three months relative to January 2026. Rubric 2 is not warranted because new licences continue to be issued and no categorical suspension has been announced.

dissent.view: Some sources (e.g. TechTimes, May 2026) note that general licences issued to three large Chinese magnet makers partially ease throughput for pre-vetted civilian customers, which could push toward a softer reading of Rubric 1; however, these general licences are explicitly not broadly available and do not constitute blanket coverage, so the overall classification remains 1.

truce_status.fact: On 23 Sep 2026, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the US and China agreed to extend their trade truce - including China's suspension of rare-earth export controls - by two months to 10 January 2027, pushing back the original 10 Nov 2026 expiry. Source: ms.now / Reuters reporting, 23 Sep 2026.
truce_status.rationale: The truce is formally extended and in force through 10 Jan 2027, well beyond the Nov-2026 nominal expiry, satisfying rubric level 0 (EXTENDED/holding). Partial compliance fraying (delayed rare-earth deliveries, June 2026 entity-list additions to MP Materials/USA Rare Earth) is noted by officials but did not prevent extension and is not sufficient to shift the reading to level 1.

dissent.view: US officials (USTR Greer, Sep 2026) state China's rare-earth deliveries 'have not been up to par' and China added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export-control entity list in June 2026 - signalling partial breach of spirit of truce.

re_blacklist.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 (June 22, 2026) added 10 named US entities to China's export control list, explicitly including MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc., barring Chinese exports of dual-use items to those firms with immediate effect. Source: MOFCOM via GlobalSecurity.org/Benchmark Minerals/Arnold & Porter, June 22-25 2026.
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) are listed by firm — satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific). The restriction covers only the 10 named entities, not the US rare-earth sector as a class, and market signals (Bloomberg: 'curbs are mostly symbolic') do not support escalation to level 2.

hree_premium.fact: Benchmark Minerals Intelligence Q3 2026 Rare Earths Price Review (published ~24 Sep 2026): 'By September, dysprosium oxide CIF Europe gained 56% to reach an average of $3,500/kg... while Chinese domestic dysprosium and terbium prices continued to retreat.' China domestic DyO reference per Rare Earth Exchanges (17 Sep 2026): ~$212-218/kg. Implied multiple: $3,500/$215 ≈ 16.3x. Terbium oxide CIF Europe $6,745/kg vs China domestic ~$996/kg ≈ 6.8x.
hree_premium.rationale: The rubric asks for the ex-China HREE price premium as a multiple of the China price; applying BMI's September 2026 CIF Europe dysprosium oxide average ($3,500/kg) against the contemporaneous China domestic reference (~$215/kg) yields ~16.3x, reflecting the extreme bifurcation driven by China export licensing controls post-April 2025. CIF North America references and lower-tier ex-China spot values yield a lower ~4.6-5.2x multiple for dysprosium, indicating geography and transaction type drive a wide spread within the 'ex-China' category.

genius_impl.fact: As of 2026-09-28, no agency has issued final rules implementing the GENIUS Act. The statutory one-year rulemaking deadline of July 18, 2026 has been missed. All major regulators remain in proposed-rulemaking (NPRM) stage: the Federal Reserve only published two NPRMs on September 24, 2026 (60-day comment window pending); Treasury published its Section 3 NPRM on August 17-18, 2026 with comments due October 19, 2026; the OCC's NPRM (published February 25, 2026) is targeting a final rule by November 2026; the FDIC approved its NPRM on April 7, 2026. CoinDesk (2026-09-24) stated: 'the agencies are all well past the legal deadline.' The GENIUS Act effective date falls back to the 18-month backstop of January 18, 2027 unless final rules are issued first. Sources: federalreserve.gov (Sept 24 2026), federalregister.gov (Aug 18 2026 / Apr 10 2026), coindesk.com/policy (Sept 24 2026), occ.gov bulletin-2026-3, fdic.gov press release Apr 7 2026, treasury.gov sb0605 (Aug 17 2026).
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric assigns 2 (PROBLEMS) when the deadline is missed without final rules. The July 18, 2026 statutory one-year rulemaking deadline has been missed by all primary federal regulators, none of whom have issued final rules; all remain in public-comment NPRMs well past that date, mapping directly to the rubric's 'deadline missed without final rules' criterion.

dissent.view: Agencies are making 'significant progress' and the overall GENIUS Act enforcement effective date (Jan 18, 2027) has not yet passed, suggesting the framework is still on track for operation — CoinDesk frames missed rulemaking deadline as procedural, not a system failure.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Q2 2026 earnings (Amazon 30 Jul, Alphabet 29 Jul, Microsoft 29 Jul): combined 2026 hyperscaler capex guidance raised to ~$730B, up ~78% YoY from ~$410B in 2025 (valueaddvc.com/ai-spending, Aug 2026). AI-attributable cloud revenue growth: Google Cloud +82% YoY to $24.8B (accelerating from +63% in Q1), AWS +37% YoY to $42.2B (fastest in 18 quarters), Azure +43% YoY; Microsoft AI business +123% YoY at $37B annualized run rate (fourweekmba.com, kucoin.com, Jul-Aug 2026). Capex growth (~78% YoY) exceeds blended AI-revenue growth for the group, but all three cloud units are accelerating YoY and no company cut its AI-revenue outlook.
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~78% YoY) materially exceeds blended AI-revenue growth (AWS 37%, Azure 43%, Google Cloud 82%), keeping the gap wide; however, AI revenue is accelerating YoY across all three platforms (Google Cloud QoQ acceleration from 63% to 82% is particularly strong) and no hyperscaler has raised capex while cutting its AI-revenue outlook, ruling out rubric level 2.

dissent.view: Sequoia/Allianz Research estimated a ~$600B annual gap between AI infrastructure spend and AI ecosystem revenue in 2025, with a ~46% capex-to-revenue divergence exceeding the 2001 telecom overbuild peak of 32% -- suggesting the gap may be worse than headline cloud growth rates imply when total ecosystem (not just hyperscaler cloud) revenue is the denominator.

gpu_refi_stress.fact: On July 29, 2026, CoreWeave (CRWV) CDS hit ~855 bps, implying ~50% five-year default probability per Bloomberg/TechTimes; within days CoreWeave had to sweeten terms to place a $2.6 billion GPU-backed leveraged loan tied to its Anthropic contracts. CoreWeave total debt stood at $35bn as of 30 June 2026 (Capacity Global, Aug 12 2026). The loan was ultimately placed but only after repricing -- no confirmed default or failed refinancing.
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: A named borrower (CoreWeave) faced a refinancing wall with CDS at distressed levels and was forced to offer improved terms to complete a GPU-backed debt transaction, satisfying rubric 1 criteria exactly. No confirmed default, distressed exchange, or truly failed refinancing has been reported, so rubric 2 is not met.

dissent.view: Some commentary (tech-insider.org, metirai.com) frames CoreWeave's structure as near-crisis given $35bn debt vs ~$6.2bn TTM revenue, implying rubric 2 risk is imminent; however no actual default or failed deal has been confirmed as of late September 2026.

DBRS/Morningstar and Bloomberg noted the $8.5bn Meta-backed GPU facility carries 'highly stable cash flows' on take-or-pay terms, suggesting the most senior GPU-backed paper remains investment-grade and not in distress.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: CRED iQ reported the office CMBS delinquency rate reached 13.2 percent in August 2026, the highest reading since at least 2019, covering $189.6 billion of office debt across conduit, SASB, and CRE CLO deals; reported by Commercial Observer on 2026-09-28 (https://commercialobserver.com/2026/09/office-cmbs-delinquency-rate-cred-iq/).
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The 13.2% figure is the most recent authoritative office CMBS delinquency reading available as of the query date (2026-09-28); Trepp-specific office data for Aug 2026 was not separately isolated in retrieved results, but CRED iQ's August 2026 figure is consistent with Trepp's own trajectory (11.13% in Sep-2025, 11.76% all-time high in Oct-2025 per Trepp) and represents the best available hard delinquency anchor.

dissent.view: KBRA office CMBS delinquency rate was 12.8% in February 2026, down from 13.9% in January 2026, using KBRA-rated private label universe only
S&P Global Ratings reported the office CMBS rate surpassed 10.5% in January 2026 for its rated universe

regional_bank_stress.fact: Five US bank failures YTD in 2026 per Forbes Advisor (Aug 24, 2026); within the trailing 6 months (Apr-Sep 2026): Community Bank & Trust-West Georgia ($288M assets) closed May 1, 2026 (FDIC.gov), preceded by a Federal Reserve enforcement action in April 2026 against its holding company citing capital and board deficiencies; separately, FDIC OIG issued a Failed Bank Review for Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust on May 29, 2026 (fdicoig.gov), with Bisnow (Feb 2, 2026) credibly reporting CRE-linked real estate loan exposure. No coordinated interagency CRE-specific emergency action found.
regional_bank_stress.rationale: At least one enforcement action (Fed, April 2026) and one FDIC OIG review within the 6-month window overlap with CRE-adjacent exposure per credible reporting, and no failure exceeded $10bn or triggered a coordinated supervisory response — fitting ISOLATED (1) rather than CALM (0) or CLUSTER (2). The Fed enforcement action did not explicitly cite CRE concentration as a primary cause, holding confidence to medium. [cross-check (asi1): two reads disagreed (1 vs 0); held for review]

govt_stability.fact: PM Sebastien Lecornu's Second Lecornu government (minority coalition, incumbent since 10 Oct 2025) survived two no-confidence motions on 23 Jan 2026 after invoking Article 49.3 to pass the 2026 budget revenue section (269 votes in favour vs 288 needed, per Euronews/Reuters/Al Jazeera); as of 17 Sep 2026, Lecornu is still PM and proposing a 2027 budget amid ongoing minority-government fragility (Bloomberg, 2026-09-17). No dissolution or collapse has been executed.
govt_stability.rationale: France's government is governing as an explicit minority relying on Article 49.3 and surviving (not falling to) no-confidence votes — the definition of FRAGILE (band 1). No snap election has been called nor has the government fallen, ruling out band 2.

rating_action.fact: S&P downgraded France from AA-/A-1+ to A+/A-1 (stable outlook) on 17-18 Oct 2025 (S&P Global Ratings press release via France24/Bloomberg/Euronews); Fitch cut France from AA- to A+ (stable outlook) in Sep 2025 (Bloomberg/FXStreet); Moody's kept Aa3 but moved outlook to negative on 25 Oct 2025 (France24). S&P reaffirmed A+ in May 2026 (Bloomberg) and Fitch upheld A+ in Mar 2026 (Euronews). Two of three Big-3 agencies executed actual one-notch downgrades within the trailing 12 months ending 2026-09-28.
rating_action.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires an actual rating cut in the trailing 12 months; both S&P (Oct 2025) and Fitch (Sep 2025) delivered one-notch cuts from AA- to A+, squarely within the window. Moody's negative outlook would independently satisfy level 1, but the executed cuts by two agencies override it to level 2.

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch Auto ABS subprime 60-plus-day delinquency index rose 33 basis points in July 2026 to 6.13%, up from 5.80% in June 2026, per CUCollector citing Fitch (published ~September 2026). The series peaked at 6.90% in January 2026 (all-time record) and seasonally retreated to 5.80% in June before reversing. KBRA's July 2026 Auto Loan ABS report independently corroborated non-prime 60-plus-day delinquency rising 19 bps month-over-month and 26 bps year-over-year.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The rubric asks for the latest subprime auto 60+ day delinquency rate as a percent; the most recent monthly Fitch ABS index figure publicly reported is July 2026 at 6.13%, which is the load-bearing fact. August/September 2026 Fitch data have not yet been publicly disseminated in the sources found, making July 2026 the latest hard figure.

dissent.view: ankso.blog (updated ~August 2026) cites May 2026 Fitch subprime 60+ DPD at 5.49% as the low point and projects mid-to-high 5% to low 6% range for remainder of 2026, implying current rate may be tracking toward or above 6%.
S&P Global reported full-year 2025 subprime auto ABS 60+ DPD at a record 6.18% average (vs. 5.78% in 2024), a distinct annual-average metric vs. Fitch's monthly index.

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm FQ3'26 Shareholder Letter (SEC 8-K, filed ~May 2026): '30+ day delinquencies excluding Peloton and Pay in X loans increased 29 basis points year over year and increased 7 basis points quarter over quarter to 2.8%.' Allowance for credit losses 6.0% of loans HFI; monthly installment loan cohorts tracking ~3.5% ultimate net charge-offs as % of GMV.
bnpl_delinq.rationale: Delinquency is up 29 bps YoY (well below the 100 bps spike threshold) and charge-offs are tracking ~3.5% ultimate NCO (below the 5% spike threshold), squarely matching Level 1: RISING with contained charge-offs. Level 2 is not warranted without a >100 bps YoY move or >5% charge-off rate.

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (data.imf.org, published ~July 1 2026): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.'
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric requires the latest published USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the IMF COFER July 2026 release gives 57.13% for 2026Q1, the most recent official observation. Q2 2026 data has not yet been published (expected ~October 2026), so 57.13 is the load-bearing figure.

dissent.view: coferdata.com displays USD at 56.77%, citing official IMF COFER figures — likely reflecting a prior quarter (2025Q4 at 56.42 per IMF, or a revised/interpolated reading) rather than the July 2026 release

weaponization_event.fact: The 18th BRICS Summit (New Delhi, 12-13 Sept 2026) unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration, which formally endorsed BRICS Pay as a decentralized cross-border local-currency settlement platform and expanded the BRICS Payment Task Force mandate; however, BRICS Pay was NOT operationally launched — leaders 'took note' and the declaration called for continued work, with no common currency created and no sovereign reserve seizure executed. On the reserve-freeze front, Russian CBR assets (~€260-300bn) remain frozen/immobilised in Western jurisdictions but have NOT been seized/confiscated; as of late September 2026 the debate remains political/legal, with the CBR filing an annulment action before the EU General Court on 3 March 2026. Sources: Irish Times (10 Sept 2026), SGT Report (Sept 2026), Forbes India BRICS 2026 takeaways, kohenavocats.com (Sept 2026), Brookings.
weaponization_event.rationale: The New Delhi Declaration constitutes official rhetoric plus a formal mandate endorsement for non-dollar settlement (BRICS Pay), placing the event squarely in Band 1 (TALK/agreement without operational execution). No new sovereign reserve seizure was executed in 2026; Russian assets remain frozen under existing 2022 measures, not newly confiscated, so Band 2 is not triggered.

dissent.view: Some media (informedclearly.com, watcher.guru) characterise BRICS Pay as already 'live' or 'operational' in 2026 with 67% intra-bloc local-currency trade; this overstates execution — SGT Report and EBC confirm the New Delhi summit leaders only 'took note' and no fully unified live system was launched.

Modern Diplomacy (Dec 2025) and kohenavocats.com (Sept 2026) describe an EU 'push' toward permanent seizure of Russian assets in September 2026; however this remains a political proposal, not an executed confiscation, so Band 2 is not met.

insurer_exits.fact: A June 2026 Climate Cosmos analysis identifies 13 states (including CA, FL, TX, NC, GA, IA, and others) experiencing active insurer non-renewal waves; NAIC's own analysis (cited in CNBC, Aug 6 2026) found non-renewal rates per 1,000 in-force policies up 96%-216% by region since 2018, with the trend continuing into 2026; however AM Best's Market Segment Report (published Sep 28 2026) documents a $16.5B underwriting gain in 2025 and describes H1 2026 as 'a calmer, more favorable start to the year,' with no top-10 insurer reported as fully exiting a major state market in 2026. Sources: climatecosmos.com (Jun 18 2026); content.naic.org / CNBC (Aug 6 2026); AM Best via financialcontent.com (Sep 28 2026).
insurer_exits.rationale: ~13 states are cited as active non-renewal/market-pressure zones, squarely in the 5-15 state range of rubric level 1; no confirmed full exit of a top-10 insurer from a major state market in 2026 (State Farm paused new business in CA but did not fully exit), and AM Best signals improving underwriting results, ruling out level 2.

dissent.view: AM Best (Sep 28 2026) reports markedly improved homeowners underwriting results in 2025 ($16.5B gain) and a calmer H1 2026, suggesting the market is stabilizing rather than still accelerating — consistent with a low-end '1' or even trend toward '0' in some states.

S&P GMI (Insurance Journal, Sep 7 2026) describes 2026 as a 'fragmented, state-by-state' phase where some states have already completed rate corrections, implying partial stabilization rather than a uniform non-renewal wave.

cat_losses.fact: Global insured natural catastrophe losses for H1 2026 totaled USD 42B (Swiss Re Institute, Aug 20 2026) to USD 47B (Aon, Jul 22 2026), vs. a 10-year H1 average of ~USD 50B (Munich Re) to USD 64B (Gallagher Re) — 28% below the decadal average per Gallagher Re. No single event exceeded USD 10B in insured losses through H1; five consecutive quarters without a >$10B event. Q3 2026 full recap not yet published. Atlantic hurricane season suppressed by El Niño.
cat_losses.rationale: H1 2026 YTD insured losses are 28-36% BELOW the 10-year average across all primary sources, and no single event has crossed the $10B threshold; this squarely maps to Rubric Score 0 (NORMAL). Absent a major Q3 hurricane or wildfire event exceeding $10B insured — of which no such event has been publicly reported by any primary source as of 2026-09-28 — the indicator remains NORMAL.

ss_reform_news.fact: The 2026 Social Security Trustees Report (released June 9, 2026, SSA.gov/oact/trsum/) projects the OASI trust fund depleted in Q4 2032 — one quarter earlier than the 2025 report — with the 75-year actuarial deficit rising to 4.42% of taxable payroll. No benefit cut has been enacted or automatically triggered; multiple reform bills (e.g., Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act H.R. 9187; PROMISE Act, July 14 2026) are in active debate but none has been signed into law.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report materially worsened the OASI depletion date (2033→2032) and widened the long-term deficit, satisfying the rubric's Band 1 condition of a worsened depletion outlook. No automatic reduction has been triggered (trust fund still solvent) and no legislation enacting cuts has been enacted, so Band 2 is not met.

dissent.view: AARP/Brookings cite the combined OASDI depletion date as 2034 (unchanged from 2025 report), which could imply no deterioration — but the action-forcing OASI-only date did move earlier (2033→2032), and the 75-year shortfall grew 16%.
CBO (February 2026) estimated a steeper automatic cut of 28% vs. the trustees' 22%, reflecting different economic assumptions, though both confirm the 2032 OASI depletion date.

pension_leverage_event.fact: TPR's Market Oversight report (thepensionsregulator.gov.uk, data through May 2025) states: 'LDI arrangements remained resilient in January 2025 when gilt yields increased during a period of higher volatility' and that 'LDI managers have maintained higher buffer thresholds, reducing leverage and improved collateral management.' ESMA mandated a 300 bps yield buffer for GBP LDI funds from April 2024 (esma.europa.eu). No forced selling or central-bank intervention has been reported in 2026; the January 2025 gilt sell-off episode resolved in an orderly manner per TPR and industry participants.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: All primary regulatory sources (TPR, ESMA, BoE FPC) confirm buffers are adequate and the system withstood recent yield spikes without forced selling or intervention; this maps directly to rubric band 0 (NONE). No evidence of any 2026 margin-call episode or regulatory stress-flag was found.

dissent.view: TPR's November 2025 report (via Isio summary) notes trustees should go further in stress-testing and diversifying collateral, implying residual pockets of concern, but stops well short of flagging systemic stress or a margin-call episode.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): the 100 largest U.S. public pension plans had a funded ratio of 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, down from 88.7% as of June 30, 2026. Source: Milliman PPFI release via BusinessWire, dated August 27, 2026 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827829119/en/).
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the highest-frequency, directly authoritative monthly tracker of the 100 largest U.S. public plans; 88.2% is the most recent published figure (July 31, 2026), making it the load-bearing number for this rubric. Equable Institute projects a slightly lower FY2026 average funded ratio of 85.0% on an actuarial basis, reflecting different methodology (actuarial vs. market-value), but both readings cluster in the mid-to-high 80s, consistent with the 88.2 PPFI value.

dissent.view: Equable Institute projects the average national funded ratio at 85.0% for FY2026 (actuarial basis, broader plan universe), up from 81.2% in FY2025, with unfunded liabilities of ~$1.13 trillion.
NASRA/Universal Asset Owners cite median funded ratios of approximately 73-75% for 2024-2025, a lower figure reflecting median vs. aggregate and older actuarial measurement dates.

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (data through end of 2025, published June 2026, emp.lbl.gov/queues): 'the median duration from IR to COD was over 5 years for projects built in 2025' — corroborated by Axis Intelligence citing the same LBNL report as 61 months (up from 36 months in 2015 and 22 months in 2008).
interconnection_months.rationale: The rubric requests the latest LBNL median queue wait in months; the 2026 Edition reports 61 months (IR to COD) for 2025 vintage projects, the most current annual datapoint available. This is a confirmed measured outcome from actual built projects, not a forecast, satisfying the top-band physical-data anchor requirement.

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed Executive Order #62 on July 14, 2026, imposing a one-year statewide moratorium on environmental permits for hyperscale data centers (>=50 MW) — the first enacted statewide moratorium in the U.S. Beyond New York, DLA Piper (July 2026) reports >100 local moratoria adopted nationwide, moratorium bills introduced in at least 11-12 states (GA, MD, MI, MN, PA, NY, OK, SD, NJ, WI, NH, and federally), and datacenterbans.com (Sept. 14-21, 2026 week) documents new local pauses enacted in at least 10 jurisdictions in a single week. (Sources: governor.ny.gov July 14 2026; dlapiper.com July 2026; datacenterbans.com Sept 2026; cnbc.com July 14 2026)
dc_moratoria.rationale: Rubric level 2 requires a statewide moratorium enacted OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses/cancellations. New York's EO #62 (July 14, 2026) is a signed, in-force statewide moratorium — satisfying the first condition alone — and is further corroborated by >100 local enacted pauses documented nationwide.

dissent.view: Maine's legislature passed a moratorium in April 2026 but Gov. Mills vetoed it; some sources (Multistate, April 2026) briefly characterized Maine as 'poised to become the first state' before the veto, which would conflict with the NY-first characterization, but post-veto sources confirm NY is first.

ai_power_pressure.fact: New York Governor Hochul issued Executive Order 62 on July 14, 2026 imposing a statewide moratorium on data center permitting citing grid cost burdens; Texas Governor Abbott on August 3, 2026 ordered PUCT and ERCOT to pause all new data-center grid connections pending a comprehensive audit -- two confirmed power-scarcity-driven moratoria. The IEA Electricity 2026 report (August 2026) simultaneously confirms >2,500 GW stalled in global grid connection queues and 'rising congestion-related curtailment' across many power systems. Sources: sheppard.com (July 29 2026), texaspowercost.com (Aug 3 2026), iea.org/reports/electricity-2026/executive-summary (Aug 2026).
ai_power_pressure.rationale: The rubric's level-2 threshold is 'a power-scarcity-driven moratorium.' Both New York (statewide executive order) and Texas (PUCT/ERCOT connection pause) have enacted exactly that within the past 60 days, with grid capacity strain explicitly cited. The IEA corroborates with evidence of rising curtailment globally.

dissent.view: FERC's June 18, 2026 tailored orders to all six U.S. grid operators are designed to 'significantly shorten the multi-year interconnection queue backlog,' suggesting policy-driven easing is underway -- but this is prospective intent, not an observed physical shortening.

LBNL Queued Up 2026 shows a 10% decrease in total active U.S. queue volume vs. prior year, driven by high project withdrawal rates rather than accelerated completions -- a signal of attrition, not relief.

mine_disruptions.fact: Three top-20 copper mines have confirmed, currently active production cuts: (1) Escondida (#1 world) fully suspended Sept 23 2026 after a fatality, only partially restarting as of Sept 25 with a strike vote pending Sept 28-30 (Crux Investor / discoveryalert.com, Sept 24-27 2026); (2) Grasberg (#2 world) still ramping up from Sept 2025 mud rush, targeting only 65% capacity in H2 2026, 2026 copper output cut to ~700 million lb vs normal 1.7 billion lb (mining.com, May 8 2026; FCX 8-K Q2 2026); (3) Kamoa-Kakula (DRC, top-5) 2026 guidance cut to 290,000-330,000 t from 420,000 t original target due to 2025 seismic/flood disruption, smelter running at 60% capacity (Ivanhoe Q2 2026 release, July 8 2026; Zijin half-year report, Aug 2026). Benchmark Minerals and ICSG both forecast a 2026 global refined copper deficit as a result.
mine_disruptions.rationale: Three named top-20 mines have confirmed, physically measurable output cuts currently active, and multiple institutions (Benchmark, ICSG) have issued deficit forecasts - this satisfies the CLUSTER threshold of >=3 mines disrupted OR lost output large enough for institutional deficit forecasts, awarding a score of 2.

dissent.view: Goldman Sachs as of April 2026 still maintained a 2026 copper surplus forecast, diverging from Benchmark and JPMorgan deficit calls

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 meeting forecast: global refined copper market surplus of ~96,000 metric tons in 2026, reversing the prior October 2025 forecast of a 150,000t deficit; driven by weaker demand growth (revised to 1.6% from 2.1%) and higher secondary/scrap output. Source: ADMIS/Recycling Today citing ICSG April 2026 release (admis.com, recyclingtoday.com, indexbox.io, April 24-28 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: The most recent ICSG annual balance forecast (April 2026) is a +96kt surplus, which clearly exceeds the +100kt threshold and maps directly to rubric level 0 (SURPLUS). A separate ICSG monthly data point showed a 51kt deficit in July 2026 (Newsquawk, Sept 2026), but this is a monthly flow, not the annual forecast called for by the rubric.

dissent.view: ICSG October 2025 forecast: 150,000t refined copper DEFICIT for 2026, driven by concentrate bottlenecks and slower production growth
J.P. Morgan projects a 330,000t deficit for 2026, driven by AI data-center and EV demand
ICSG monthly data (July 2026): refined copper market posted a 51kt supply deficit in that single month, suggesting actual 2026 flows may be running toward deficit

drought_chip_farm.fact: USDM map released 2026-09-24 (data valid 2026-09-22) shows drought improved in the West; as of 2026-09-01, ~33.6% of Arizona is in D2 (Severe) drought and ~0% in D3, with 10 of 12 major Reclamation reservoirs below average as of 2026-08-30 (drought.gov, 2026-09-16). Taiwan imposed water rationing at chip-hub Hsinchu County through July 2026 (Taipei Times, 2026-03-27) but no confirmed active rationing or fab curtailment is found for September 2026.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: The US Southwest is currently dominated by D1-D2 (Moderate-Severe) drought with western conditions improving per the latest USDM release, meeting rubric band 1 (EMERGING). The Taiwan water-rationing order that affected Hsinchu in spring 2026 has not been confirmed as still active in September 2026, so level 2 cannot be assigned on current evidence.

dissent.view: Arizona long-term drought remains D3-D4 in every county per AZWATER.gov (as of mid-2026 review), which would argue for rubric level 2 on a long-term structural basis

Taiwan Water Resources Agency imposed confirmed water rationing at Hsinchu County (chip fab hub) effective through July 2026 - a level-2 qualifying event in spring 2026 that may not yet be fully resolved

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,037.79 ft, 26.13% of capacity (191.21 ft below full pool of 1,229 ft), per USBR gauge data via water-data.com/lakemead and corroborated by Colorado River Monitor (26.1%, Sep 27) and USBR Weekly Hydrologic Update Aug 31 (26%, 1,038.22 ft). Hoover Dam minimum power pool is 1,050 ft — lake is currently ~12 ft BELOW that threshold.
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.13% of capacity, Mead falls below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL floor; it is also operating approximately 12 feet below Hoover Dam's 1,050-ft minimum power pool threshold, confirming confirmed physical impact to hydropower generation — satisfying both CRITICAL triggers simultaneously.

dissent.view: reservoirs.earth (using NID design capacity of 28.26 maf rather than USBR operational capacity of 26.12 maf) reported 24.4% as of Sep 5, 2026 — a lower percentage due to different capacity denominator, but directionally consistent with CRITICAL classification

water_dispute.fact: Two active disputes: (1) GERD/Nile — Egypt reaffirmed at UNGA on 26 Sep 2026 that Nile water is a 'non-negotiable existential priority'; Ethiopia's army chief accused Egypt of backing Tigray rebels as of 27 Sep 2026 (Euronews/AP); Egypt's MoD has active operational strike plans vs. GERD (Atalayar, Aug 2026); diplomacy frozen, no binding treaty, no direct kinetic action or deliberate flow cut-off confirmed. (2) Indus — India kept treaty in 'abeyance' since Apr 2025, rejected Hague Court of Arbitration ruling of 31 Aug 2026 that treaty 'remains fully in force' (Al Jazeera/Bloomberg, 1 Sep 2026); Permanent Indus Commission has not met since May 2022; Pakistan's Defense Minister made conditional war statement in June 2026 (CNBC, 22 Jun 2026).
water_dispute.rationale: Both disputes are at rubric level 1: the Indus Waters Treaty is formally suspended/contested by India despite an international ruling, and the GERD dispute features official war threats and proxy-conflict accusations exchanged at the UN level — but no confirmed armed clash between riparian states over the dams/rivers, nor any deliberate flow cut-off, has been documented, keeping both below the level-2 threshold.

dissent.view: Some analysts (Atalayar, Aug 2026; African Arguments, Sep 2026) characterize Egypt's documented military strike planning and proxy encirclement of Ethiopia as crossing into de facto conflict-level behavior that could merit a '2' classification.
Other analysts (FPRI, Oct 2025; pppescp.com, Mar 2026) assess armed conflict likelihood as 'relatively low' given the structural and logistical constraints on Egypt projecting force against GERD.

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 1.9 percent from its revised July level (131.1) and 2.5 percent higher than a year earlier, reaching its highest level since end-2022. Source: FAO official newsroom release, 4 September 2026 (https://www.fao.org/newsroom/detail/supply-concerns-drive-fao-food-price-index-higher/en).
fao_food_trend.rationale: MoM change of +1.9% is above zero (rising) and YoY is +2.5% (rising), satisfying ELEVATED criteria; however, MoM is well below the 5% SPIKING threshold and the 3-month gain (Jun 130.3 to Aug 133.3) is ~+2.3%, far below the 10% trigger, so rubric maps to 1.

china_export_curbs.fact: China's 2026 urea export quota stands at 3.3 million tonnes (vs ~5 Mt shipped in 2025), paired with minimum FOB price floors of $430-440/t (most destinations) and $500/t for India; phosphate (DAP, MAP, NPK) exports remain suspended per the NDRC December 2025 directive, extended at least through August 2026, with the quota-and-price-floor mechanism confirmed still reshaping Q4 nitrogen markets as of September 18, 2026 (Fertilizer Daily, https://www.fertilizerdaily.com/20260918-china-urea-export-quota-2026-nitrogen-price-floor/).
china_export_curbs.rationale: Active urea quotas with binding FOB price floors plus phosphate export suspension (NDRC-directed, December 2025, extended through August 2026) confirm restrictions remain in place. The only broadening event - the March 2026 ban on NK blends and additional phosphate varieties - occurred ~6 months ago, outside the trailing 3-month window required for a rating of 2, so the rubric maps to 1 (IN PLACE, unchanged in the last 3 months).

dissent.view: China reportedly lifted fertilizer export curbs specifically to India in August 2025 per a diplomatic assurance from FM Wang Yi, suggesting a partial bilateral carve-out rather than a general restriction
Philippines reported China indicated fertilizer exports would not be restricted broadly, though Chinese authorities did not publicly confirm this

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-20 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; Brent crude at $106.31 as of 02:53 UTC on 28 Sept 2026, up 1.91% on the day after Trump rejected Iran's seven-day reopening proposal; WTO-AXSMarine Strait of Hormuz Trade Tracker (early September 2026) shows fertilizer shipments 'near zero' with outbound ammonia, urea and sulfur flows not materially recovered. Sources: straits.live/briefs/2026-09-28 (28 Sept 2026); fertilizerdaily.com/20260911 (11 Sept 2026).
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: The strait is physically rated CLOSED (2): PortWatch records 1 transit/day vs. 85 pre-crisis, fertilizer/sulfur/ammonia flows are near zero per WTO-AXSMarine, and crude oil at $106/bbl corroborates the closure signal. No signed truce or operating convoy system is in place as of today - Trump rejected Iran's reopening proposal on 28 Sept - so the rubric cap at 1 does not apply.

dissent.view: Lloyd's List Intelligence (9 Sept 2026) counted 346 non-Iranian-linked transits in August and an 82-transit week ending 30 Aug, suggesting some partial recovery/volatility rather than a total halt, though still far below the pre-war 3,000/month baseline.

taiwan_tension.fact: Taiwan's MND official press release (Sep. 5, 2026) confirmed 20 PLA aircraft sorties—including J-11, Su-30, H-6 bombers, Y-8EW and KJ-500—of which 12 crossed the median line entering northern, central and southeastern ADIZ sectors in a 'joint combat readiness patrol'; a follow-on patrol on Sep. 9 extended coverage to Taiwan's northern, central and eastern airspace. China Coast Guard 'law enforcement' patrols east of Taiwan have been ongoing since July 2026. No kinetic clash or blockade was reported. (Sources: ROC MND press release mnd.gov.tw Sep. 5 2026; ISW-AEI China & Taiwan Update Sep. 11 2026; The Diplomat Sep. 22 2026)
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent median-line crossings, multi-type aircraft joint readiness patrols, and regularized CCG patrols east of Taiwan fit rubric level 1 (elevated: large-scale assertive patrols/blockade rehearsals, no kinetic clash). Overall sortie volumes remain below the 2024-2025 peak, precluding a level-2 read absent any blockade or kinetic event.

dissent.view: ISW-AEI (Sep. 1 2026) notes monthly PLA ADIZ incursion totals are less than half August 2024/2025 levels and have reverted to pre-Lai baselines since start of 2026, suggesting strategic de-escalation rather than escalation—a lower-intensity read within level 1.

export_controls.fact: In the trailing 3 months: (1) US BIS on June 1 2026 issued a guidance rule extending semiconductor export controls to Chinese-owned entities outside China (Al Jazeera/BIS, 2026-06-01); (2) the MATCH Act (proposing DUV lithography ban) advanced in Congress as of July 2026 (CNBC/Reuters, 2026-04-07; Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-14); (3) China promulgated 'Regulations on Countering Improper Extraterritorial Jurisdiction' in April 2026 (Just Security, 2026-07-09) and escalated rare-earth export controls in June-July 2026 with NdPr benchmark prices up ~21% month-on-month to ~$133/kg in July 2026 (Tech-Insider, ~2026-09-07), constituting formal countermeasures with price-signal corroboration.
export_controls.rationale: Both sides have enacted active measures in the trailing 3 months: the US via a BIS enforcement rule and MATCH Act advancement (tightening), and China via a formal counter-jurisdiction regulation and escalated rare-earth controls with confirmed price signals (retaliation). Two active escalation counts — one on each side — maps to rubric level 2.

dissent.view: East Asia Forum (2026-03-11) characterised the Trump White House as 'cooling down' chip controls, suspending the Affiliates Rule and relaxing H200 licensing, suggesting the executive branch was de-escalating even as Congress pushed harder — this would support a lower reading if only executive actions are counted.

fab_concentration.fact: TSMC Arizona Fab 1 (N4/4nm) is the sole operational overseas fab, producing ~10,000-30,000 wpm but NOT at <=3nm; Arizona Fab 2 (N3) construction complete with tool install Q3 2026 and HVM targeted H2 2027; Japan JASM Fab 2 (3nm) HVM 2028; all <=3nm capacity (~180,000 wpm 3nm + ~90,000 wpm 2nm = ~270,000 wpm) remains in Taiwan as of Q4 2026. TSMC CFO Q1 2026 earnings: overseas capacity ~2-3% of total. Sources: TSMC.com Arizona page (July 2026); CNBC/Wendell Huang July 2026; TrendForce Sept 14 2026; TechTimes Aug 8 2026; siliconanalysts.com April 2026.
fab_concentration.rationale: Zero operational <=3nm capacity exists outside Taiwan as of September 2026: Arizona Fab 1 runs N4 (4nm) and Fab 2 (N3) and Japan Fab 2 (3nm) both target HVM in 2027-2028 at earliest. This satisfies both conditions of rubric level 2: <10% outside Taiwan AND no operational overseas leading-edge fab.

dissent.view: Once Arizona buildout is complete (~2028-2030), Wei projects ~30% of 2nm-and-below capacity in US — used by some analysts as evidence of imminent diversification — but this is a forward projection, not a current operational fact.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 1 vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz on 20 September vs a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day; Reuters-cited data showed 10 commodity vessel crossings on 23 September vs a 10-day average of ~17. Iran's IRGC declared the strait closed to 'unfriendly nations' from 2 March 2026 onward; US-Iran reopening talks are ongoing but unresolved as of 28 September. Brent crude is trading at ~$104-108/bbl on 28 September 2026, up ~59% year-on-year — a market signal fully consistent with a near-closure. (Sources: cargolinked.com 25-Sep-2026; straits.live 27-Sep-2026; tradingeconomics.com 28-Sep-2026; fortune.com 28-Sep-2026)
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Transit volume at ~1-10% of the pre-crisis baseline (well under the 25% threshold) with Brent ~$105-108/bbl — ~59% above year-ago levels — satisfies the rubric's dual condition for a rating of 2: physical near-closure corroborated by an oil price signal consistent with severe supply disruption. Active but deadlocked US-Iran talks do not constitute a 'functioning convoy workaround' or a signed truce, so the 1-cap rule does not apply.

dissent.view: CargoLinked (25 Sep 2026) notes some Iran-approved vessels (mostly petroleum bound for China/India) are still transiting with military escort, and CENTCOM says non-Iranian commercial traffic 'may continue' — implying partial rather than total closure, which could support a rating of 1 (contested).
GoFreight (Jul 2026) characterises the Red Sea as merely 'contested' with CMA CGM running limited naval-escorted routes, which would support a rating of 1 for that corridor specifically.

cable_incidents.fact: The PEACE submarine cable was cut in the Red Sea (~1,450 km from Zafarana, Egypt), reported July 27, 2026 by Data Center Dynamics/Submarine Cable Networks; repair expected to take 'several months' due to cable-ship capacity crunch — status unrepaired as of late September 2026. Separately, Iran issued explicit threats in mid-September 2026 to cut Hormuz undersea cables (Asia Times, Sept 16, 2026), and the September 6, 2025 multi-cut event (SMW-4, IMEWE, FALCON/GCX) near Jeddah had extended repair timelines. The Australia-Singapore Cable also broke on Sept 4, 2026 (Indonesia-Singapore segment, partial reroute only as of Sept 18).
cable_incidents.rationale: At least one named major cable (PEACE, Red Sea) is confirmed severed and unrepaired months after the cut, satisfying rubric level 2 ('>=1 major cable currently severed and unrepaired causing connectivity loss'). Iran threats to Hormuz cables add a simultaneous threatened-vector, but the PEACE cut alone meets the level-2 threshold.

dissent.view: TeleGeography/submarinecablemap.com (updated Sept 22, 2026) lists many cables as 'in-service' and does not flag an active multi-system outage at Red Sea level comparable to Sept 2025 severity; the Sept 2025 cuts (SMW-4, IMEWE, FALCON) may have been substantially repaired by mid-2026, leaving only PEACE as confirmed unrepaired.
AGBI (March 2026) and TeleGeography (April 2026) frame Hormuz cable risk as elevated threat, not an actual cut — no confirmed severance at Hormuz.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: SIFMA/BNY/Broadridge/DTCC June 2026 Pulse Survey (340 experts, released 22 Sep 2026): 'The survey suggests the industry is positioned well for the cash implementation but there remains considerable work to do as the industry prepares for the repo deadline.' 86% are at least somewhat confident of meeting the overall mandate; 88% of deferred programs cite legal/contract-negotiation as driving delays; 72% say they need more regulatory clarity; 51% have no formal backup plan; pending exemptive-relief requests (SIFMA inter-affiliate, IIB cross-border) were still open for public comment as of Aug 2026 per SEC Commissioner Uyeda statement (sec.gov, Aug 7 2026); TBAC Q2 2026 charge (May 2026) flags documentation backlog for done-away bilateral agreements as 'the largest challenge from an implementation standpoint.' Cash deadline Dec 31 2026 appears on track; repo deadline Jun 30 2027 has 'considerable work' remaining. (Sources: dtcc.com press release 22 Sep 2026; sec.gov Uyeda statement 7 Aug 2026; home.treasury.gov TBAC Q2 2026 charge May 2026)
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: The rubric scores 1 (FRICTION) for documentation backlog or pending exemptive relief or readiness surveys <60% 'very confident.' The June 2026 survey confirms an active documentation/legal backlog (88% of delayed firms cite contract negotiation) and unresolved exemptive-relief petitions still in SEC comment as of Aug 2026; while the cash deadline looks achievable, the repo leg shows material execution gaps — matching the FRICTION definition precisely. No deadline extension or major operational failure (score 2) has occurred.

dissent.view: NY Fed President Williams (cited in Cryptobriefing ~Sep 2026) characterised the transition as 'ahead of schedule,' and a DTCC GSD member survey showed most respondents 'already prepared or actively completing final readiness activities' for the Dec 31 cash deadline, suggesting the cash leg alone might score 0 (SMOOTH).
